Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you to possible hypertension, but they don't provide actual readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but require periodic calibration with a traditional cuff blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to provide full blood pressure measurements without any calibration, supported by a trial involving thousands of people……

"The Silent Killer"

Both abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) pose significant health risks.

Of the two, high blood pressure is more dangerous and is known as the "silent killer" because it can cause serious, irreversible damage to the arteries, heart and brain without any obvious symptoms. The condition often only comes to light when it triggers a heart attack or stroke.

Especially for older adults, regular blood pressure monitoring is advisable, and home cuff-style monitors are widely available for self-measurement. However, being able to monitor automatically through a fitness device already worn would of course be the ideal scenario.

Apple Watch Blood Pressure Feature

With the launch of watchOS 26, five Apple Watch models can measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models will not provide any readings, and will only alert you when signs of possible high blood pressure are detected. Other devices such as the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices do offer actual blood pressure readings, but they require regular calibration against measurements from a cuff-style monitor.

Signal Ring

Start-up company Vital Signals says it has developed a smart ring called the Signal Ring that requires no calibration and matches the accuracy of traditional arm-cuff blood pressure monitors.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Moss said he nearly died from undiagnosed high blood pressure, which led him to found the company.

The ring is available for pre-order later today, ships in October, is priced at US$399, with no subscription required. The companion app (see above) displays real-time blood pressure readings and long-term trend tracking.

It is worth noting that the Oura Ring has not yet received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials showed it delivered accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss has no plans to sell the ring to all consumers. He said the ring's professional features are best suited to older adults and those assessed by doctors as being at risk of high blood pressure, implying that the Signal Ring may fall short in other areas such as sleep tracking.
